entry: RestClient, WebClient and WebTestClient request exchange

questions.history: Run this history with RestClient, WebClient and WebTestClient, keeping URI, handler and request defaults fixed.
questions.prediction: Expect the new derivative to send [one,two] on both revisions. A fresh derivative of the base is expected to leak two before and send only [one] after for each name.
questions.basis: The PR demonstrates the original RestClient cookie list acquiring two. Each derived configuration starts from the same original defaults.
questions.refutation: The landed base derivative sends two, or the edited derivative loses either value.

fix.return: rest=[one, two]/[one, two]/[]/[] -> [one]/[one]/[]/[] web=[one, two]/[one, two]/[]/[] -> [one]/[one]/[]/[] test=[one, two]/[one, two]/[]/[] -> [one]/[one]/[]/[]

questions.history: Using fresh fixtures, add a previously absent header X-Extra and cookie extra only to the derived builder.
questions.prediction: On both revisions the original should omit both names and still send its initial values.
questions.basis: The previous copy already allocated distinct maps. Adding a new key distinguishes map sharing from value-list sharing.
questions.refutation: The new name reaches the original or its previous value disappears.

questions.history: Build WebTestClient A from a retained builder. Append two to the builder’s existing header list and cookie, build B, then GET from A after B.
questions.prediction: On the landing A should send just one for both names while B sends one and two. The PR describes parent leakage into clients already built.
questions.basis: A's public build boundary precedes the change. Capturing actual requests independently tests the snapshot clients consume.
questions.refutation: A sends B's later values, or B sends only A's original values.

parent.return: B=[one, two]/[one, two]/[]/[] A=[one, two]/[one, two]/[]/[]
